answers.answer: Each player takes 12 ordinary turns: three per season across four seasons. A courtship is an event with no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’; ‘Courtship is an event, with no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.’

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate service (Quarters to Available, then Expended to Quarters); resolve the round event; resolve applicable ongoing monument/Servants’ Hall effects; choose an activity; invite the exact required gentry; provide all required service; resolve all positive favours before negative favours; optionally buy; clean up. At cleanup, used servants go to Expended Service, played gentry to your personal discard, and the activity tile returns to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. Only the last player advances the marker after cleanup.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, ‘Hosting an activity’: numbered steps 1–8; Player Reference ‘Host’.

answers.answer: Passing order: all servants directly to Available Service; all gentry in your discard to hand; round-track event, then ongoing effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; the last player advances the marker. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: ‘all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase’.

answers.answer: Yes. Screening is fixed at the end of step 2, when reputation is 6.1, so it qualifies for the PR6 tile and guests. Four Service Help actions may then lower actual reputation to 3.4 without invalidating them. Each Service Help moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service, at a cost of 3 reputation increments; it cannot take one directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening is ‘fixed at the end of step 2’; later changes ‘without invalidating the activity.’ Service Help moves one servant from Quarters to Available.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; order within those groups is otherwise your choice. At minimum reputation, you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to avoid a loss; negative losses stop at 1.1. A money penalty must be fully payable, using positive activity money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money if needed; if you cannot fund it, you cannot play that guest/tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6: ‘all positive favours before all negative favours’; money penalty paragraph; minimum-reputation rule.

answers.answer: Borrow Money costs 2 reputation increments and gives £100; repeatable. Service Help costs 3 increments per servant moved from Quarters to Available; repeatable. Refresh Market costs 4 increments and is limited to once per turn as a special action. At minimum 1.1, you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot move a servant directly out of Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special actions table and minimum-reputation paragraph.

answers.answer: Host the Butler’s Room with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service; there is no hiring fee. The used butler also goes to Expended Service and the tile upgrades on first use. Once upgraded, instead of hiring up to two from supply, recruit one common footman, valet, or lady’s maid from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service. Unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: ‘Butler’s Room’ entry under Servants and hiring.

answers.answer: A housekeeper substitutes for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman substitutes for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman) even if that servant type is still available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: substitution rules.

answers.answer: Acquire an underbutler only by purchasing Butler’s Pantry; it enters Expended Service immediately. It normally moves to Quarters at your next rotation and to Available Service at your second subsequent rotation. Passing or a Refresh Service VP card can make it available earlier; once in Quarters, Service Help or Servants’ Quarters can allow earlier use. Another player cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.
answers.evidence: Butler’s Pantry paragraph under Servants and hiring.

answers.answer: Pay the Market space price plus the tile’s printed modifier; in Reserve the base price is £300 plus the modifier. Price cannot go below £100. You may not acquire a duplicate tile you already own. Reputation does not restrict purchases, so you may buy above your reputation.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: ‘Pay the market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier. Reserve base price is £300’; minimum £100; duplicate and reputation rules.

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. A drawn duplicate stacks on its matching Market tile and another tile is drawn. Reserve-eligible draws go directly to Reserve and are replaced by another draw. If multiple spaces are filled, sort only the newly drawn Market tiles by sorting number. Taking one tile from a duplicate stack leaves that space occupied, so it does not trigger a refill.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve, ‘Refill’ paragraph.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service draws also go directly there, with the same exception. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve; later PR1 draws go there too. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. The full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard; refresh the Market after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: ‘Open Reserve’ and ‘Refresh’ paragraphs; Overview confirms full seasonal refresh is standard.

answers.answer: For ordinary courtships 1–3, return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall, wherever held. Sum tile VP in the current theme’s face-up category, including negative VP and only the face-up hybrid category. The highest scorer gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild. If tied for highest, each tied player draws a VP card and nobody gets a Fairchild. Each player discards one objective; simultaneous discards are shuffled together and placed face down on the objective deck’s bottom. Then pass the first-player marker anticlockwise.
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep, ordinary courtship steps 1–4 and seasonal upkeep sequence.

answers.answer: At final courtship, return Fairchilds and score tile VP across all four revealed themes; a repeated category counts repeatedly, including negative VP. Highest gets one VP card and a Fairchild. Tie is broken by highest reputation level (wheel position ignored); if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied players draw VP cards. Discard the final objective, then players get a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits before the marker moves to Wedding Bells and final scoring.
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep, ‘Final courtship (round 16)’.

answers.answer: Final VP comes from face-up improvement-tile VP (including negatives), printed gentry VP in hand and discard (including family and final Fairchild; dismissed guests excluded), fulfilled remaining objectives, reputation level, servants, wealth, and retained VP cards. Reputation levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP. Wealth is 1 VP per £200, rounded down. Ties: final Fairchild holder wins; otherwise highest reputation level; if still tied, share victory. Wheel position has no effect.
answers.evidence: Final VP table and tie rule.

answers.answer: Normally deal five objectives at setup and draw two on round 6. Discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Additional objectives from Main Library or a VP card increase the retained final count and do not create an extra discard. Shuffle simultaneous discards together, then put them face down on the bottom of the objective deck. Tile objectives require owning the named tiles at game end; they need not be upgraded.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards paragraph.

answers.answer: A VP card can be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your own later turn (multiple cards may be used), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard it to use its benefit; used cards go to the VP deck’s bottom. Retained unused cards stay hidden with objectives and score their printed VP; you cannot take both benefit and final VP.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: VP card rules.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after its first use; an already-upgraded normal tile stays upgraded after later uses. A hybrid starts with its underlined icon showing and flips after every use. A tile that upgrades into an ongoing monument (Queen’s Suite or Lionheart Suite) hosts once, upgrades to a monument, and never hosts again. Only a hybrid’s currently face-up category counts for courtship and objectives.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: normal tiles, hybrids, monuments; base objective reference.

answers.answer: Resolve monuments and Servants’ Hall in the ongoing-effects step after the round event: step 2 when hosting, step 3 when passing. Each monument gives one reputation per ordinary turn, hosting or passing, but none during courtship; a newly purchased monument pays on a later turn. Servants’ Hall lets you place one available servant to reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one reputation; that servant goes to Expended at turn end and cannot serve the activity. Do not target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects; hosting and passing order.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite uses one footman on the tile and one casual guest from hand, with the guest’s normal service; double all that guest’s favours, including negative ones; it upgrades and stays an activity tile. Queen’s Suite uses a housekeeper and one prestige guest from hand, with normal guest service; double one chosen favour and resolve others normally; it upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite uses a butler and draws one prestige guest from the deck to attend, requiring no personal guest service; double nonnegative favours, excluding negative favours from doubling; keep the guest and put it in your discard at cleanup; it upgrades into a monument. Each suite has a fixed one-guest count that cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: ‘Suite activity’ table and following fixed-count sentence.

answers.answer: A random player receives the first-player marker. Starting with the player to that player’s left and proceeding clockwise, players choose available base family boards. Bonuses: Asquith adds the Dowager Countess as a fifth family card; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York adds a footman to Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Each player starts with reputation 1.1 except Cavendish at 1.4 after its bonus. Stack the 1/2, 3/4, 5/6, and Max counters with 1 showing and Max at the bottom; do not use 7/8 counters. Starting Available Service: one butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid, and footman. Starting tiles: Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour, Bowling Green, with starter/building icon showing. Ordinary family cards: Lord, Lady, Heir, Young Lady. Only Ponsonby starts with money (£300); the other families start with none. Asquith additionally has Dowager Countess; York also gets a footman.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2, 3, and 5.

answers.answer: For three players, place 3 valets, 3 lady’s maids, 6 footmen, and 2 underbutlers total in Servants for Hire. No butlers or housekeepers are included. Unused servants are returned to the box and unavailable for the game.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6: one valet and lady’s maid per player, two footmen per player, two underbutlers total; absent types and boxed servants specified.

answers.answer: Separate starter guests from the casual deck, shuffle them, and deal two to each player’s hand. Shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests remain casual guests during play, with a starter icon, and otherwise follow normal casual rules.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Gentry, screening, dismissal and family.

answers.answer: For four players, select one double-sided monument per player plus one, so five total. Choose at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Put selected monuments and all nonstarter base improvement tiles in the draw bag. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments always go in the bag and do not count against the five selected monuments.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Fill six different Market spaces with eligible tiles: PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set ineligible draws aside and return them to the bag after filling; stack duplicate eligible tiles in the same space. Normal tiles enter with upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids with underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort spaces by ascending sorting number, beginning at the £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall, and double-sided monuments are ineligible.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Set Alderley Hall standard side up and round marker at 1; put one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal the first theme and keep revealed themes in order. Place base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild face up on Alderley Hall. Thus the first theme is open, not hidden, and revealed themes remain in order rather than leaving play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9; Overview says revealed themes are kept in order through the game.

answers.answer: At hosting-turn rotation, a servant in Quarters moves to Available Service; one in Expended Service moves to Quarters. Each advances exactly one space. An available servant you do not use remains available.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 1: ‘Unused available servants remain available’; rotation order.

answers.answer: No immediate Village Fair reward if Private Study is not already upgraded when the event resolves; upgrading/hosting it later that turn does not grant the missed reward. An already-upgraded Study gives £300 and 2 reputation. Village Fair occurs on standard spaces 3 and 9.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table, Village Fair row; Private Study paragraph says upgraded side reward on Village Fair rounds only.

answers.answer: Resolve the round-track event before ongoing tile effects: on a hosting turn after service rotation, and on a pass after servants and discarded gentry return. On space 6 draw two objectives and keep both secret with your other objectives. The event applies to each player’s turn, including a passing player.
answers.evidence: Round-track events intro and table; Draw Objectives row.

answers.answer: Yes. National Holiday waives PR on all tiles and guests when hosting, so low-reputation players may play higher-PR ones. All other requirements remain, including service and gentry counts/types.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table, National Holiday row.

answers.answer: Yes, Builders’ Holiday permits any number of Market and/or Reserve purchases within funds. Finish all purchases before sliding/refilling; the Market remains unchanged at existing prices, with each price based on its original space (or Reserve price) plus printed modifier. No refresh between purchases by special action or VP card. Refill all resulting empty spaces together afterward. Market Purchase VP cards follow the same single-unchanged-market/no-refresh rule.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table; Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card paragraph.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside, leave Reserve unchanged, and refill all six Market spaces from the bag under normal refill rules (sorting new tiles by number). Only after refill, return the set-aside tiles to the bag and mix; they cannot reappear in that same refresh. Reserve tiles stay as they are.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve, ‘Refresh’ paragraph.

answers.answer: Each reputation symbol is one increment. Moving clockwise across position 5 to 1 raises a level; moving anticlockwise across 1 to 5 lowers one. The minimum is 1.1 and maximum is 7.5 (Max.5); losses beyond 1.1 are ignored. At Max.5, excess gained reputation is otherwise lost, unless spent immediately on special actions; you can take actions before or during a reputation favour to make space.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions opening paragraphs.

answers.answer: Money held is public. Players may not give or receive money between them. You may never spend more than you hold; a money penalty must be fully payable. The common supply is unlimited, using proxies if necessary.
answers.evidence: Money held paragraph and money penalty paragraph.

answers.answer: Ladies includes every female family member or female guest, so family can fill a ladies requirement. A casual-guest requirement requires casual guests and excludes family. You must play exactly the printed number and types; no extra gentry. Family has no PR and needs no personal service. Guests and activity tiles must meet screening PR unless National Holiday waives it.
answers.evidence: Hosting steps 4–5; reputation screening paragraph.

answers.answer: For an ordinary guest-invite favour, draw one card from the indicated deck, reveal it to everyone, and add it to hand; the draw does not attend the current activity. For a screening invite, draw the stated number, choose the stated number to keep, reveal only kept cards and add them to hand. Put rejected cards unseen on the bottom of their guest deck.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family: invite table and screening paragraph.

answers.answer: Dismissal is optional, so you need not dismiss if you have no unwanted guest. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, current activity, or discard, including one just drawn by an earlier favour. Family cannot be dismissed. Put the dismissed guest on the bottom of its matching deck; it is no longer yours, will not return on passing, and does not score for you.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family, dismissal paragraph.

answers.answer: Lord gives £200. Lady offers a choice: screen two casual guests and keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir offers a choice of £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager gives both £100 and one reputation.
answers.evidence: Base family card favour table.

answers.answer: The Young Lady gains the admirer bonus only with a male prestige guest attending the same activity: two reputation. A male casual guest does not qualify; a female prestige guest does not qualify; Charles Fairchild does qualify because he is a male prestige guest. In every case the Young Lady still draws one casual guest.
answers.evidence: Base family card favour table and Charles Fairchild ruling.

answers.answer: Charles is a male prestige guest with no PR, requires a valet, and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a female prestige guest with no PR, requires a lady’s maid, and gives both one prestige guest and two reputation. They are guests, not family, so neither has family dismissal immunity; either may be dismissed under the normal guest rule.
answers.evidence: Gentry paragraph on Fairchilds; Elizabeth and Charles favour sentences.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one; Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and makes you lose one reputation. A player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: base gossips; reputation section: minimum protection.

answers.answer: The Barn gives one reputation each time you host an Estate activity. Owning an Estate tile alone and passing give no reputation from the Barn.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects, Barn paragraph.

answers.answer: Ordinary rotation moves all Quarters servants to Available, then all Expended servants to Quarters, one space each, at hosting-turn start. The Servants’ Quarters improvement lets you use one servant still in Quarters after rotation directly, in addition to Available Service, with no reputation cost; send it to Expended at turn end. Service Help instead costs 3 reputation per servant and moves one Quarters servant to Available; it cannot move from Expended.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring service-mechanism table; ordinary rotation paragraph.

answers.answer: The front-side Private Study requires two family and a butler and has no tile favour. After it upgrades, its ongoing effect gives £300 and two reputation on Village Fair rounds only; you do not host it again to collect the reward. The summary does not explicitly state whether the front-side activity can be hosted repeatedly before its first upgrade; it says normal activity tiles must upgrade after first use, which means the front side is used once before it flips.
answers.evidence: Private Study paragraph; normal activity tiles must upgrade after first use.

answers.answer: Unupgraded Main Library requires a butler and two family and draws one extra objective. Upgraded Main Library requires a butler and three family and draws one VP card. Extra objectives increase the number retained for final scoring; they do not cause an extra discard.
answers.evidence: Main Library paragraph; Objectives and VP cards paragraph.

answers.answer: The Objective VP card draws two objectives, keeps one, and puts the other on the bottom of the objective deck. It adds one retained objective to your final objective count.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table, Objective row.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants, including those in Expended Service, directly to Available Service for immediate use. Service Help costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves only one servant from Quarters to Available; it cannot take one from Expended.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table, Refresh Service row.

answers.answer: A Hire Servant VP card takes one servant from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service. Because it enters Expended Service, it cannot immediately provide service under normal availability; it must advance through service rotation unless another stated effect makes it available sooner.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table, Hire Servant row; service rotation rules.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest may return any one gentry, including a family member, from personal discard to hand. If returned before attendee selection, you may then play that card for this activity if it meets the normal requirements; the card does not attend automatically.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table, Refresh Guest row.

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets, and lady’s maids; it excludes butler, housekeeper, and underbutler. Ordinary service VP is 2 VP for every servant of every type and location. The ten-servant objective awards 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: basic-servant and servant-set rows; Final VP table, Servants.

answers.answer: Yes. Upgraded Queen’s Suite counts as an Estate tile and as a monument; upgraded Lionheart Suite counts as a Prestige tile and as a monument. Thus each can count toward both its category objective and monument objective. A hybrid counts only in its currently face-up category.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: monument/category explanation and hybrids sentence.

answers.answer: Nature Group is worth 11 VP and requires Flower Room plus one garden: English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is worth 12 VP and requires Gabled Conservatory plus one of Main Library or North Library. Owning the tiles at game end is enough; they need not have been used or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference, Nature and Domestic Group entries; tile objective rule.

answers.answer: The prestige-guest objective counts prestige guests; the summary says prestige guests include a final Fairchild. The every-three-guests objective counts all nonfamily guests, so guests of any guest category count and family does not. It scores one VP per complete group of three; an incomplete group scores nothing.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: Guest bonuses; prestige guests include final Fairchild.

answers.answer: The base reputation objective awards 7 VP for maximum reputation level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective awards 10 VP for at least £1200. Ordinary reputation VP is based on reputation level (levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28), not wheel position; reputation-level ties likewise ignore wheel position.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Final VP table and final tie rule.

answers.answer: West Terrace requires one butler and exactly three family on both sides. Unupgraded it draws one prestige guest. Upgraded it draws one prestige guest and may optionally dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to their decks’ bottoms. It remains an activity tile and never becomes an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: base West Terrace paragraph.

answers.answer: There is no hand or personal-discard limit. Gentry in your discard still belong to you and score normally; passing returns them to your hand.
answers.evidence: Gentry section opening sentence.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles at any time and buy any one, including one underneath another in a stack; you are not limited to the top tile. Every Reserve tile is public. Normal price, duplicate, and purchase limits still apply.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve paragraph.

answers.answer: You may choose to host or pass; the summary does not require hosting whenever legal. If your preferred activity lacks required gentry or service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure overview; Hosting steps 4–5.

answers.answer: Yes. On a passing turn you may use the free Market refresh benefit, one paid special-action Market refresh, and multiple Market Refresh VP cards, each of which refreshes separately. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the paid special-action Refresh Market; the free pass refresh and VP-card refreshes do not use that allowance. Market refreshes cannot interrupt a Builders’ Holiday/Market Purchase buying sequence.
answers.evidence: Special actions paragraph on refresh methods and multiple cards; Builders’ Holiday purchase restriction.

answers.answer: No. Special actions are available at any time on your own turn, while hosting or passing; they are not available as interrupts during another player’s turn.
answers.evidence: Special actions: ‘available at any time on your own turn, hosting or passing’.

answers.answer: No. Favour effects are mandatory unless expressly optional; the printed guest invite must be resolved, so you cannot decline it while taking other favours. An optional dismissal is different: you may choose not to dismiss, and dismissal itself is always optional.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6: favours mandatory unless expressly optional; dismissal paragraph says dismissal is always optional.
